title: Japan — Northern Alps in autumn
notes: Fifteen nights, sequenced north to south and high to low so it follows the autumn colour down the mountain rather than fighting it, opening with a night at Nagano for Zenkoji and closing with two in Tokyo. The dates are a deliberate trade: Hakuba's alpine colour peaks late September, the Nakasendo's peaks late October, and five weeks apart they cannot both be caught in one trip — so this window takes Hakuba at its best and accepts the Kiso valley before its peak and Kamikochi in maples rather than golden larch. Happo Pond decided it: reported at peak on 11 Oct in both 2024 and 2025, and it gets three nights and two headline walks here. The cost is Sports Day on 11 Oct, which the trip is arranged around rather than against: the holiday weekend is spent in Nagano, a city, and the drive over to Hakuba happens on the Monday itself, against the traffic heading home. Nothing is booked yet. Every remark on this page comes from the file and is replaced whenever the plan changes; the private notes behind sign-in are yours and are never written to from here.

summary.note: Budget figures are the whole trip for two travellers, in MYR, and are planning estimates rather than quotes — nothing is booked. They exclude flights. The exchange rate is the mid-market rate on 14 Aug 2026 (1 MYR = 38.9 JPY), a placeholder until money is actually changed; every converted figure on the site moves with it. Day costs carry only fares that have been looked up and checked, as a group total for two, so the daily totals are well below what a day will really cost — the planning envelope is this table, not those. Shopping is deliberately not here and is tracked separately; Miscellaneous is contingency, not a shopping allowance.

days.summary: Arrival only — nothing planned, so the first full day starts rested.

items.activity: Check in at KLIA for NH886
items.remarks: Three hours before a 14:15 departure.

items.activity: Fly Kuala Lumpur (KUL) to Tokyo Haneda (HND)
Land at Haneda, clear immigration and collect bags

Travel to the hotel
Haneda (HND) -(Walk)> Hotel
items.remarks: Airport hotel — the late landing is deliberate and there is nothing worth a train ride at this hour.

days.summary: Tokyo to Nagano, and an afternoon at Zenkoji.

items.activity:
Travel to Tokyo Station
Hotel -(Tokyo Monorail)> Hamamatsucho Station -(JR Yamanote Line)> Tokyo Station
items.remarks: About 17 minutes on the monorail from Haneda Terminal 3, then 5 on the Yamanote — allow 30 with the change and the bags. The Keikyu line to Shinagawa and JR across is the same journey by another route if the monorail is queued.

items.activity:
Travel to Nagano
Tokyo Station -(Hokuriku Shinkansen)> Nagano Station
items.remarks: Three services run this line and they are not interchangeable. Kagayaki is fastest at about 80 minutes but is entirely reserved — there are no unreserved cars at all, so turning up hoping to board one does not work. Hakutaka takes about 95 minutes and Asama, which terminates at Nagano, a little longer; both carry unreserved seats. JPY 8,340 per person reserved, JPY 7,680 unreserved — figure shown is reserved for two. No oversized-baggage reservation is needed here: that rule covers the Tokaido, Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen only, and the Hokuriku is first come, first served.

items.activity: Check in, then lunch at Nagano
items.remarks: Nagano is soba country. One night here rather than a bus-gap stop, which is what turns Zenkoji from a rushed hour into an afternoon.

1,400 years old, and it holds the first Buddhist statue ever brought to Japan — kept hidden, never shown. The part people remember is the kaidan meguri: a pitch-dark passage under the main hall where you feel along the wall for the key to paradise. JPY 1,200 per person for the combined ticket, JPY 600 for just the inner sanctuary and passage; figure shown is the combined for two. Allow two hours inside, plus another for the approach street. About 15 minutes by bus from the station, or 30 on foot straight up the main road.

If tomorrow's bus is a late one, Zenkoji holds a morning service at dawn — 05:30 to 07:00 depending on sunrise, led by the head priests, and one of the few daily temple rituals in Japan still open to the public. A better hour there than any afternoon.

days.summary: Five shrines up a mountainside, through 400-year-old cedars.

items.activity:
Travel to Togakushi
Nagano Station -(Alpico Bus)> Togakushi Okusha
items.remarks: Just over an hour, JPY 1,550 per person each way; figure shown is the return for two. Green season runs eleven departures a day from Nagano Station, 06:50 to 14:10, so this is a far easier bus than the Hakuba one. Three things the operator is specific about: every seat is reserved (book online, which opens a month ahead — you can board without one if there is space, but not reliably), Suica and the other IC cards do NOT work so bring cash or a contactless Visa, and the old Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass was discontinued in 2025, so do not plan around it.

items.activity:
Walk the cedar avenue to Okusha
Togakushi Okusha -(Hike - 40 mins)> Togakushi Okusha Shrine
items.remarks: A 2 km approach through the thatched Zuijinmon gate and then 300-odd Japanese cedars, many of them 400 years old. The cedars are evergreen, so the avenue looks the same whatever the date — which is the point today, because Togakushi sits at about 1,200 m and peaks late October, so the colour around it will only be turning.
Togakushi is one of Japan's three great soba regions. Eaten here with sansai tempura — battered mountain vegetables.

The middle shrine, about 40 minutes down through the forest from Okusha. Carry on another 2 km to Hokosha for the full five-shrine walk, or stop here — the whole traverse is 10-12 km. Use the Togakushi Shuttle Bus to move about within the area.

items.activity:
Travel to Nagano
Togakushi Chusha -(Alpico Bus)> Nagano Station
items.remarks: Last bus of the day leaves the campsite at 16:20 and reaches Nagano at 17:25. Earlier ones run roughly hourly through the afternoon.

days.summary: Over to Hakuba on the holiday, and a terrace above the valley.

items.activity: Collect the hire car at Nagano Station
items.remarks: The car covers the next four days - Hakuba, Matsumoto and Azumino - and goes back at Matsumoto. Both are in Nagano prefecture, which is the whole point: a one-way drop inside one prefecture is free or close to it, where Nagano to Nagoya would have run to tens of thousands.

items.activity:
Check out and drive to Hakuba
Nagano Station -(Drive)> Hakuba Station
items.remarks: About 1h 15m, and deliberately on Sports Day itself. The holiday traffic on a Monday runs the other way - people leaving the resorts for the cities - so going north into Hakuba is against the flow, and tonight is the first quiet night in the valley after the long weekend rather than the last busy one. The rental desk will be busy with returns, so allow a little longer at the counter.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags

Explore Hakuba Iwatake Mountain Harbor
Hotel -(Drive)> Hakuba Iwatake Mountain Resort
items.remarks: The gentle option for an arrival afternoon: the Noah gondola climbs eight minutes to a terrace at 1,289 m looking straight across at the Northern Alps, with THE CITY BAKERY and a couple of other places to eat on the deck. Green season runs 08:30-17:00 with the last ride up at 16:20 and the last down at 16:50, and the bakery shuts at 16:00 - so this is an afternoon, not an evening.

Hakuba Happo Onsen is highly alkaline at pH 11 and over, and is Japan's only natural hydrogen hot spring, which is what the silky-water reputation is about. Four public baths if the hotel has none of its own: Happo-no-Yu (JPY 1,000, 10:00-21:00, daily), Obinata-no-Yu (JPY 700, 11:00-21:00), Mimizuku-no-Yu (JPY 1,000 but only 13:00-17:00 for non-guests) and Sato-no-Yu.

days.summary: The classic Hakuba walk, on the best date the trip can give it.

items.remarks: Start early. The trail is high and completely exposed, and the light on the Alps is best before the afternoon cloud builds.

items.activity:
Travel to Happo-one
Hotel -(Drive)> Happo Gondola Adam
items.remarks: Ten minutes or so from most of the village, with parking at the gondola base.

items.activity: Ride the Alpen Line to Happo Ike Sanso
items.remarks: Three stages - the Adam gondola, then the Alpen Quad and Grat Quad chairlifts - about 20-25 minutes in total, ending at the Happo Ike Sanso lodge at roughly 1,830 m. JPY 3,500 per person return for the full line; figure shown is for two. Check the last descent before you start walking: uphill service stops 30 minutes before the final Grat Quad, and the green season ends on 3 Nov.

items.activity:
Hike to Happo Pond
Happo Ike Sanso -(Hike - 90 mins)> Happo Pond
items.remarks: 3.3 km round trip and about 230 m of climb, to the pond at 2,060 m. Just above the lodge the path forks and it is worth knowing which is which: the LEFT branch is mostly wooden boardwalk and much easier underfoot, the RIGHT is rocky and uneven. They rejoin higher up, so take the boardwalk going up and decide about the rocks on the way down. Estimates vary widely - the operator's own guide says 1.5 to 2 hours up and an hour down, other sources say 45 minutes; budget two hours and be pleased if it is less. Cairns mark the way and there is a small stone shrine at the pond.

The reflection is the whole point, so it wants a still morning. This is also why the trip sits where it does: the pond was reported at peak on 11 Oct in both 2024 and 2025, so today is a single day past two years of observed peak, and on an ordinary Tuesday rather than yesterday's holiday. Two warnings from the operator worth repeating - the trail has no shelter at all from wind or rain, so windproof layers are not optional, and it wants proper hiking shoes rather than trainers.

items.activity:
Return to Hakuba
Happo Pond -(Hike - 60 mins)> Happo Ike Sanso
items.remarks: About an hour down, then the lifts. If this morning was clouded in, today and tomorrow's Tsugaike can swap - that is the only spare card the three nights hold.

days.summary: Six kilometres of boardwalk over four marshes, at your own speed.

items.activity:
Travel to Tsugaike
Hotel -(Drive)> Tsugaike Kogen
items.remarks: About 25 minutes north, and the clearest case for having the car up here - the bus to Tsugaike is sparse.

items.activity: Ride the gondola and ropeway to Tsugaike Nature Park
items.remarks: The Eve gondola takes about 20 minutes, then the ropeway another six, landing near the Visitor Center at roughly 1,900 m. JPY 3,700 per person return including park entry, or JPY 3,300 if bought at a Seven-Eleven beforehand - figure shown is the gate price for two. The Visitor Center runs 08:30-16:40 and the park closes for the season at the end of October. Confirm the gondola is not in its late-October maintenance window.

Around 6 km of raised boardwalk across four marshes - Mizubasho, Watasuge, Ukishima and Tenbo. Pick the length to suit the day: there are 1 km, 2 km and 3 km circuits as well as the full 5.5 km loop, which takes about three and a half hours. Watasuge Marsh is the one to reach - the wetland opens out and the Hakuba range stands straight behind it. Boardwalk throughout, so this is walking rather than climbing, and it reads far better in flat light than Happo Pond does, which is why it is the one to move if the weather forces a swap.

items.activity:
Return to Hakuba
Tsugaike Kogen -(Drive)> Hotel

items.remarks: Last night in the valley - worth trying whichever of the four public baths you did not use on the first evening.

days.summary: Down the valley with a wasabi farm on the way, and the car goes back.

items.activity:
Check out and drive to Azumino
Hakuba Station -(Drive)> Daio Wasabi Farm
items.remarks: About 1h 15m south down the valley. Azumino sits directly on the road from Hakuba to Matsumoto, so this is a stop on the way rather than a detour - which is the whole reason the wasabi farm sits on today rather than tomorrow. It saves a there-and-back drive, a day on the hire, and the Matsumoto parking night entirely.

Japan's largest wasabi farm - 15 hectares, free to enter, laid out along clear spring-fed channels with the Alps behind. Its own best season is late Sep to late Oct, so this lands well. The wasabi soft-serve is the thing people come for. Opens at 09:00; the closing time shifts with the season, so check before relying on a late finish.
Wasabi soba at the farm itself, or into Hotaka for something more substantial.

Optional, and the first thing to drop if the day runs long: the Rokuzan Art Museum is beside Hotaka station and the Chihiro Art Museum a little further out. Azumino is also 30 minutes from Matsumoto by train, so anything missed today can be picked up on a spare morning without a car.

items.activity:
Drive to Matsumoto
Daio Wasabi Farm -(Drive)> Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: About 35 minutes. Refuel on the way in - full-to-full is the usual policy.

items.activity: Return the hire car at Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: Four days, and a day earlier than this plan used to have it. Because the car goes back before check-in, there is no Matsumoto parking to arrange at all, and a 16:00 drop leaves real margin against the branch's closing time - the old 17:30 did not. Everything from here is walking, rail or bus: Kamikochi bans private vehicles and the Magome-Tsumago walk is point-to-point.

Local to the city rather than generic: sanzoku-yaki (a whole garlic-soy chicken thigh, fried), basashi, and Shinshu soba - this is one of Japan's best buckwheat regions and the new crop lands in autumn.

days.summary: A whole day in the castle town, all of it on foot.

items.remarks: One of only twelve original keeps left standing in Japan, and a National Treasure. JPY 1,200 per person; figure shown is for two. Open 08:30-17:00 with last admission at 16:30. The keep is climbed by stairs only and they are narrow and steep - go up early, before the queue on them builds.

A few minutes' walk from the castle and worth pairing with it: an 1876 schoolhouse in the Japanese-Western hybrid style of the period, a National Treasure in its own right, reopened in Nov 2024 after three and a half years of earthquake-proofing. JPY 400 per person, 09:00-17:00, last entry 16:30. Combined tickets with the castle exist and save JPY 200-400 - ask at whichever you reach first.

White-walled kura storehouses with black lattice, now craft shops, cafes and sake merchants. Nawate-dori - the frog street along the Metoba river, with nostalgic toy and snack stalls - runs parallel a block north, so the two are one walk.

items.activity: Explore Matsumoto City Museum of Art
items.remarks: Yayoi Kusama is from Matsumoto and the museum holds her work, with the dotted pieces outside. This is also the wet-weather anchor for today, though the whole day is town and holds up in rain.

days.summary: Over the Abo pass to Hirayu, the car parked, and one night inside the valley.

items.remarks: Pack an overnight bag for Kamikochi and leave the cases in the car, which waits at Hirayu until tomorrow. The walk in from Taisho Pond is 3.7 km and there are no coin lockers anywhere in the valley.

items.activity: Collect the hire car at Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: The second hire: four days, collected here and handed back at Nakatsugawa on the afternoon of the 19th — it does the Abo pass, the wait at Hirayu while Kamikochi is done on the shuttle, Okuhida, and the drive down the Kiso by way of Narai, and is gone before the walk day. That crosses from Nagano into Gifu, so a one-way fee applies: JPY 18,700 including tax for a passenger car from this branch to Nakatsugawa Ekimae, on Toyota's own simulator. Toyota's Nagano list rate for a compact is JPY 8,580 for the first 24 hours and JPY 7,260 a day after. The branch is about three minutes from the station, behind the bus terminal, and opens 08:00 to 20:00. Ask the two questions the first hire asked: whether winter tyres are fitted by mid-October, since the Abo pass and Okuhida run high, and whether an ETC card comes with it.

items.activity:
Drive to Hirayu Onsen
Matsumoto Station -(Drive)> Hirayu Onsen
items.remarks: About 1h 15m up the Azusa on Route 158 and through the Abo Tunnel, JPY 790 for a car — JPY 550 on the ETC late-night or holiday discount. The old Abo pass road over the top is free and adds 25 to 30 minutes, and is worth it only for its own sake. This is the leg the bus did in 1h 25m for JPY 3,000 a head on four departures a day with compulsory seat reservations; the car buys that back. Leave the car at the Akandana car park, JPY 600 a day, which is where cars bound for Kamikochi stop: private vehicles are banned beyond Nakanoyu. Two days on the meter, today and tomorrow — worth a thought about what is left visible in the car overnight. Sawando, on the Matsumoto side, is the nearer gate, but whether its shuttle now needs booking could not be confirmed; the Hirayu shuttle certainly does not.

items.activity:
Travel to Kamikochi
Hirayu Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Taisho Pond
items.remarks: About 25 minutes through the Abo tunnel. Buy a return rather than two singles — JPY 2,800 per person against JPY 1,500 each way, so the pair saves JPY 400, and tomorrow's ride out is then already paid; figure shown is the return for two. The shuttle runs roughly every 30 minutes and cannot be reserved or bought in advance — pay at the Hirayu counter and join the queue. It runs 17 Apr to 15 Nov only. Get off one stop early, at Taisho Pond, rather than riding on to the terminal: the walk in from there finishes at the hotel instead of doubling back to it.

Dead trees standing in still water under Yakedake, which made the pond in 1915 by damming the Azusa when it erupted. The volcano still steams, and on a calm morning the whole range doubles in the surface. The far end of the valley and the quietest of its three set pieces. This is a Saturday, and October weekends are Kamikochi's busiest: the crush is roughly 10:00 to 14:00 around Taisho Pond and Kappa Bridge, which is exactly when this walk happens. It thins out through the afternoon, and dusk and tomorrow's dawn belong to the people staying.

items.activity:
Walk in to Kappa Bridge
Taisho Pond -(Walk - 75 mins)> Kappa Bridge
items.remarks: 3.7 km of flat boardwalk and gravel along the river, 75 minutes without stopping and a good deal more with. It passes the Tashiro marsh and Tashiro Pond, then the Weston monument — the plaque to the English missionary who talked Japan into climbing these mountains for pleasure. Mobile signal is patchy and exists only around the terminal, Kappa Bridge, the visitor centre, the Weston relief, Tashiro Pond and Taisho Pond.

The bus terminal and the hotels around Kappa Bridge are the only places to eat, and there is no convenience store and no ATM in the valley at all. Cards are usually taken but carry cash — the Myojin gate tomorrow is coins only.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags
items.remarks: Fewer than ten properties in the whole valley, and most serve half board because there is nowhere else to eat once the day-trippers have gone. Cancellation typically runs about 30 per cent from three days out and 50 per cent on the day, so this is a booking to be sure of before making.

Free, open until 17:00, a few minutes upstream of Kappa Bridge on the right bank. Exhibits on how the valley was made and what lives in it, and the place to ask what the Myojin path is actually doing before walking it tomorrow.

On these dates the valley is in maples rather than larch: the maple peak is around 17 Oct, so today is a day before it and about as good, while the larch does not turn gold until 25 Oct to 5 Nov and will barely have started. That is the trade the earlier window makes — red rather than gold — and it is real rather than a technicality. Putting Kamikochi ahead of Okuhida moved this from the day after the maple peak to the day before it — close to a wash. The densest larch stands, for reference, are around the bus terminal and Konashidaira.

The last buses out are late afternoon and the valley empties behind them — this is the whole reason to sleep here, and on a Saturday the contrast with midday is at its sharpest. Sunset is about 17:10, but the walls are high and the floor loses the light well before that.

days.summary: Dawn on the Azusa, a loop to Myojin, then one waterfall and up into the ryokan.

items.remarks: Sunrise is around 06:00 and the floor of the valley stays in shadow long after the Hotaka range above it has gone pink — that gap is the picture, and it is the morning the night here was for. Kappa Bridge looks straight at it; Taisho Pond adds the mist. Dress for it: this is about 1,500 m in the middle of October and the morning bears no relation to yesterday afternoon.

Check-out is usually 10:00, so it happens before the walk rather than after it. If you would rather not carry the overnight bag round Myojin, the bus terminal's baggage room takes it from 06:00 to 17:00 for JPY 350 to 600.

items.activity:
Hike to Myojin Pond
Kappa Bridge -(Hike - 60 mins)> Myojin Pond
items.remarks: 5.5 km there and back and about two hours' walking by the official figure, flat the whole way — call it three with stops. Go up one bank and back the other: the right bank is the wide main path, the left is quieter and runs through the nature-research forest. The pond is inside the grounds of Hotaka Shrine's inner shrine and is not free — JPY 500 per person, cash only, figure shown is for two. The Kamikochi tourist site still lists 300, so carry coins for either. Kamonji-goya beside it has been grilling char over an open hearth for a century.

items.activity:
Travel to Hirayu Onsen
Kamikochi Bus Terminal -(Nohi Bus)> Hirayu Onsen
items.remarks: About 25 minutes, on yesterday's return ticket. This is the quiet advantage of leaving westwards: the Hirayu shuttle takes no reservations at all, where every seat on the Matsumoto-bound bus has had to be booked a month ahead since 2025. Collect the car at Akandana. It is Sunday midday, so expect a queue for the shuttle; it runs about every half hour.

items.activity:
Explore Hirayu Great Falls
Hirayu Onsen -(Drive)> Hirayu Great Falls
items.remarks: 64 m of water off the flank of Norikura, one of Japan's hundred famous waterfalls. The car park is free and holds about a hundred, and it is roughly 20 minutes on foot from there to the falls; it closes once the snow comes, which is not a worry in October. Late October is when the falls look best — the gorge colours later than the tops do, so this is one of the few things the earlier dates do not shortchange. The ropeway is tomorrow, and if this afternoon is the clearest of the three it can come forward instead — it is 15 minutes on from Shin-Hotaka and the falls do not need a view.

items.activity:
Drive to Shin-Hotaka Onsen
Hirayu Great Falls -(Drive)> Shin-Hotaka Onsen
items.remarks: About 30 minutes up the valley. The road threads all five Okuhida villages in order — Hirayu, Fukuji, Shin-Hirayu, Tochio, then Shin-Hotaka — so another village's bath is now a short drive rather than an hourly bus.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags
items.remarks: Two nights in one place, and the point of them is the ryokan's own water rather than touring the valley. Okuhida is said to have more open-air baths than anywhere else in Japan, so choose the property for its rotenburo. Parking at a ryokan up here is normally free and normally plentiful, but it is worth confirming when booking rather than arriving and hoping.
After a 05:45 start, this is where the long day ends — in the ryokan's own bath rather than at a rental desk.

days.summary: Up Japan's only double-decker ropeway, then back down through the trees.

items.activity:
Drive to Shinhotaka Ropeway
Shin-Hotaka Onsen -(Drive)> Shinhotaka Ropeway
items.remarks: A few minutes further up from the village. Today is a weekday, so the October timetable runs from 08:45, with the last car up at 16:15 and the last down at 16:45; weekends start at 08:15 because they are busier, which is half the point of doing this on a Monday. The municipal car park at the base is gated and charges JPY 800 for each six hours for a car — it went up from 600 in June 2026 — with the first 30 minutes free and 113 spaces. Expect two blocks today. The Nabedaira Kogen car park higher up is JPY 600 a day if the base is full.

Two ropeways and a short walk between them. No.1 lifts you from Shinhotaka Onsen station at 1,117 m to Nabedaira Kogen at 1,305 m; you cross to Shirakabadaira at 1,308 m and take No.2 — the double-decker, the only one in Japan — up to Nishi-Hotakaguchi at 2,156 m. About 25 minutes all in. No.1 leaves at :00 and :30 past the hour and No.2 at :15 and :45, so the connection is built in. JPY 3,800 per person return for both; figure shown is for two. Seasonal hours shift — confirm the last descent before you go up. If the top is clouded in, tomorrow morning is the spare: 08:45 up on a weekday, back down by about 11:00, and Narai still gets its afternoon.

The rooftop observation deck gives a 360-degree sweep of the Northern Alps - Nishi-Hotaka, Yari and Kasagatake all from the same spot. There is a cafe and a panorama lounge inside for when the wind gets old, which it will: this is 2,156 m in the middle of October, so expect near-freezing and a real chance of early snow. The colour is on the lower stages rather than up here.

Back down to the middle station and into the trees: a 2.3 km loop through the Nabedaira Kogen forest, flat and easy, and the part of the day that is actually autumnal rather than alpine. Guided walks run but need booking ahead.
The Alps Bakery at the middle station does fresh bread, and there is a gelato shop and a view lounge beside it.

There is an open-air bath at the middle station, and a footbath on the platform where you can sit and watch the gondolas come and go. Bathing at 1,300 m with the Hotaka range in front of you is the sort of thing this valley is for.

items.activity:
Drive to the hotel
Shinhotaka Ropeway -(Drive)> Shin-Hotaka Onsen

items.remarks: Last night in the valley. If you have been meaning to try another village's water, the hourly bus makes Tochio or Fukuji an easy hour.

days.summary: Out of Okuhida, a proper stop at Narai-juku, and down the Kiso to Nakatsugawa.

items.remarks: An unhurried morning. If yesterday was clouded in at the top, this is the ropeway's spare: the first car up is 08:45 on a weekday and you can be back down by about 11:00, which costs Narai an hour but not the visit.

items.activity:
Drive to Narai-juku
Shin-Hotaka Onsen -(Drive)> Narai-juku
items.remarks: About two and a half hours: half an hour down the valley to Hirayu, back through the Abo Tunnel (JPY 790) to Matsumoto, then south on Route 19 through Shiojiri — Narai sits on the road about 35 km past Matsumoto, so it is a stop on the way rather than a detour. The old town is closed to cars; leave the car in one of the free car parks by the Kiso-no-Ohashi bridge or at the roadside station. The station car park (JPY 500) and the Gonbei car park (JPY 510) are the fallbacks.

The Nakasendo post town dropped earlier in the planning for want of a day, back now because the car drives past it. Nakamura-tei, the merchant house that is its main museum, opens 09:00 to 17:00 with last entry at 16:30, so go there first; the tourist office shuts at 16:00 and many shops close by early evening, which is the real limit on this stop. About two and a half hours as planned — the reason for putting Okuhida after Kamikochi. If the morning went on the ropeway instead, it is closer to an hour and a half, which is still enough for Nakamura-tei and the main street. This is a car stop for a reason: the Shinano does not call at Narai, and the station has no lockers and holds cases only until 16:00.

items.activity:
Drive to Nakatsugawa
Narai-juku -(Drive)> Nakatsugawa Station
items.remarks: About 79 km south on Route 19, an hour and a half to an hour and forty — a 50 km/h single carriageway for much of the way, so do not plan on less. Refuel on the way in; full-to-full is the usual policy, and it is easier before you reach the station than after.

items.activity: Return the hire car at Nakatsugawa Station
items.remarks: Toyota Nakatsugawa Ekimae, about two minutes from the station — cross at the crossing to the right of the exit and it is on the ground floor of the red brick building. It closes at 20:00, which leaves about three hours of slack, or two if the morning went on the ropeway; if the day runs long, cut Narai short rather than the drive. Four days, and the JPY 18,700 one-way fee settles here. Handing it back today rather than on the 21st saves a day's hire and two nights of hotel parking, and the car has no job on the walk day that the train and bus cannot do. The cases then walk the two to seven minutes to the hotel with you.

Down from about 1,100 m in Okuhida to about 340 m. Stay by the station: the car went back beside it this afternoon, tomorrow starts on the train from it, and the Tokyo train leaves from it on the 21st. No parking to arrange — the car is gone before check-in. A city of about 79,000 with business hotels a few minutes' walk away, and The Ryokan O — 120 years old and about two minutes from the station — if the room should have some character. Room only is the point: the evenings are for eating out.

The town's own Nakasendo post town — the 45th of 69, once the area's commercial centre. The old road starts at the Shinmachi crossing, about 100 m down the main street from the station, and keeps its crooked, squared-off layout and houses with udatsu, the raised firewalls that marked a wealthy family. This is also chestnut country: Nakatsugawa is where kurikinton comes from, and more than a dozen shops sell it from September into winter, so the dates land squarely in season.
The reason for sleeping here rather than in Tsumago — a choice of restaurants, rather than whatever the minshuku serves at six.

days.summary: Eight kilometres of the old Nakasendo, uphill from Tsumago to Magome, and a bus straight back to town.

items.activity:
Travel to Tsumago
Nakatsugawa Station -(JR Chuo Line)> Nagiso Station -(Bus)> Tsumago
items.remarks: The 07:41 local towards Matsumoto passes Nagiso at 08:11, which leaves half an hour for the 08:40 bus, in Tsumago at 08:47. JPY 330 per person on the train and JPY 300 in coins on the bus; figure shown is both, for two. This is the one connection the day hangs on: the next pairing is the 10:19 train with the 10:30 bus, two hours later. The 08:14 local terminates at Nagiso about 19 minutes on, a tight but workable backup for the same bus. If both are missed, walk it — Nagiso Station to Tsumago is about 3.5 km on the old Nakasendo, roughly an hour through the edges of the town and the fields rather than on stone paving, or about JPY 2,000 by taxi. Times are the current timetables; check the 2027 ones, and that the 07:41 runs on a Wednesday.

Preserved rather than restored, and the first place in Japan to try it — the village saw off the 1960s by hiding its wiring and aerials and by agreeing to sell, lease and destroy nothing. One JPY 700 ticket covers three buildings of the Nagiso Town Museum, 09:00 to 17:00: the honjin where the daimyo's party slept, the waki-honjin Okuya beside it with its cypress interior, and the history museum behind. Okuya shuts on the second and fourth Thursday of the month; the 20th is a Wednesday, so that never bites. Figure shown is for two. Arriving before the day coaches is the morning version of what sleeping here would have given, and the museum opens at 09:00 as you finish the street.

items.activity:
Hike the Nakasendo to Magome
Tsumago -(Hike - 3 hours)> Magome
items.remarks: About 8 km, two to three hours at a leisurely pace, signposted in English. Walked from Tsumago for the way home rather than for the walking: it ends in Magome, which is part of Nakatsugawa and has a direct bus back, where the other direction ends on a bus and a train with hour-long gaps between them. The price is the climb. Tsumago sits at about 420 m and the pass at 801 m, and from Tsumago the trail winds up the hillside over many switchbacks for most of the way before dropping to Magome — Kiso's own tourism office and japan-guide both say the Magome-to-Tsumago direction has less uphill. It is still graded easy to moderate; just start it with water and without hurry. The bells on posts along the trail are bear bells and are there to be rung. Around halfway is the Tateba teahouse, an old farmhouse with an open hearth where volunteers pour tea for nothing — a well-placed stop on the climb — and a 250 m detour reaches the Odaki and Medaki falls, the male and female pair. This is the day the earlier window costs something: the Kiso valley colours late October into early November, so the 20th catches it arriving rather than at its best. The cedars, the stone paving and the teahouse do not depend on the date.

A steep stone-paved street rebuilt after fires in 1895 and 1915 — a reconstruction where Tsumago is a preservation, and it still works. Water wheels, a lookout at the top of the slope over the ranges and Mt Ena, and Shimazaki Toson's family home, now the Toson Memorial Museum (JPY 500 per person, 09:00 to 17:00). Magome is in Gifu — the pass you came over was the prefectural border.

items.activity:
Travel to Nakatsugawa
Magome -(Kitaena Bus)> Nakatsugawa Station
items.remarks: About 25 minutes, JPY 800 per person; figure shown is for two. No connection to make and no hurry: weekday departures from Magome leave at 12:50, 13:50, 14:50, 15:50 and 16:50, then 17:50 (weekdays only) and 18:15 — so the time given here is only a suggestion. No reservations; pay cash on the way off, and the change machine takes JPY 1,000 notes but nothing bigger.
After eight kilometres and a hill, a restaurant of your own choosing is exactly the point of basing here.

days.summary: Out of the Kiso valley and into Tokyo, with two days still to spend.

items.remarks: Nakatsugawa-juku before checking out, or a last round of the kurikinton shops to take something back — chestnut sweets are the town's own.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Tokyo
Nakatsugawa Station -(JR Shinano Limited Express)> Nagoya Station -(Tokaido Shinkansen)> Shinagawa Station
items.remarks: About 50 minutes to Nagoya on any Shinano, then 1h 40m on. JPY 12,530 per person all in — JPY 7,150 of fare and JPY 5,380 of reserved surcharges; figure shown is for two. Every Nozomi stops at Shinagawa, which is the Haneda end of Tokyo: getting off there rather than at Tokyo Station saves a leg with the luggage, and is why the hotel is on that side. The second leg is the Tokaido, so unlike the Hokuriku on day 2 the oversized-baggage rule applies — a case whose height, width and depth total 160-250 cm needs a free reserved slot booked with the seat, and boarding without one is a JPY 1,000 charge. Measure before this leg, not at the gate.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags

items.remarks: About 15 minutes from Shinagawa. The Uniqlo and Muji flagships, Ginza Six, and Itoya for stationery.

days.summary: The night the shorter Okuhida stay bought, and deliberately still open.

items.remarks: This is the day freed by dropping the third Okuhida night, and it is left open on purpose rather than filled with something plausible. What whoever picks it up has to work around: Ginza was done on arrival yesterday and Tokyo Station is the last afternoon, and Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ueno and Asakusa have all been seen on earlier trips, so none of them is the answer here. It also lands straight after an 8 km walk and four hours of trains, which is an argument for a slow start rather than against one. The hotel is at the Shinagawa end, so anything on the Yamanote's western half or down the Yokosuka line is close.

days.summary: A last day in Tokyo, hands free.

items.activity: Check out and leave the luggage at the hotel
items.remarks: Standard and usually free at a Japanese business hotel — confirm it at check-in rather than on the morning, because the whole day rests on it. Haneda's own coin lockers and baggage counter are the fallback.

Held open alongside yesterday, for the same later round. Shibuya and Asakusa were the old plan for this slot and both have been seen on earlier trips, so they come out rather than stay in as filler. Whatever replaces them has to work with the cases at the hotel desk and be back at Shinagawa by early evening.
Character Street and the Daimaru food halls are the best single stop for edible souvenirs and ekiben.

items.activity:
Collect luggage, then travel to Haneda
Hotel -(Keikyu Airport Line)> Haneda (HND)
items.remarks: About 15 minutes from Shinagawa on the Keikyu, or 13 on the monorail from Hamamatsucho.

items.activity: Check in at Haneda for NH885
items.remarks: Three hours before a 23:30 departure.

items.activity: Fly Tokyo Haneda (HND) to Kuala Lumpur (KUL)
items.remarks: Lands 06:00 the next morning.

transport.mode: Mixed on purpose, and two hire cars rather than one. The first takes the middle four days — Nagano to Hakuba, the Hakuba trailheads, then Matsumoto and Azumino — collected at Nagano Station and returned at Matsumoto, both in Nagano prefecture so the one-way drop stays cheap. The second runs four days from Matsumoto on 16 Oct and is handed back at Nakatsugawa on the afternoon of the 19th: over the Abo pass to Hirayu, where it waits while Kamikochi is done on the shuttle — private cars are banned there — then Okuhida, and finally Narai-juku and the Kiso valley on the way down. It crosses into Gifu, so it carries a JPY 18,700 one-way fee. What it buys is the cases riding in the boot rather than being forwarded out of a mountain valley, the Kamikochi-to-Kiso leg without doubling back, and Narai, where the Shinano does not stop. It goes back on arrival because it has no job on the walk day that the train and bus cannot do. Rail for the walk day and at either end, because the long hauls are faster by train and a car is useless in Tokyo.

legs.route: Hakuba to Azumino to Matsumoto, then return the car
Matsumoto to Hirayu Onsen, then the car waits at Akandana
Hirayu Onsen to Hirayu Great Falls, then Shin-Hotaka Onsen
Shin-Hotaka Onsen to Narai-juku, then Nakatsugawa — return the car

todo.task: Book Kamikochi, 16 Oct (Sat)
todo.remarks: Do this first. Fewer than ten properties in the valley and the colour weeks sell out months ahead. Half board is the norm — there is nowhere else to eat after dark. Cancellation typically runs about 30 per cent from three days out and 50 per cent on the day, so be sure before booking. It is now a Saturday night, the hardest of the week to get in colour season. If Saturday cannot be had, swap Kamikochi and Okuhida back — Kamikochi on Mon 18 Oct, Okuhida 16-18 Oct — which is how the plan stood before 16 Sep 2026.

todo.task: Book Nakatsugawa, 19-21 Oct
todo.remarks: By the station — the car is handed back beside it on the afternoon of the 19th, the walk day starts on a train from it and ends on the Magome bus back to it, and the Tokyo train leaves from it on the 21st. No parking needed: the car is gone before check-in. Room only; the whole reason for this over Tsumago is eating out. Business hotels are a few minutes' walk away, and The Ryokan O, 120 years old, is about two minutes from the station for something with more character. Tsumago's minshuku had a few rooms each; a station-side hotel is not a scarcity booking in the same way, so this drops down the order behind Kamikochi.

todo.task: Book Okuhida onsen ryokan, 17-19 Oct
todo.remarks: Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. Pick for the bath rather than the room — two nights, and the only thing the plan leaves the property for is the ropeway. Confirm parking too, now that the car comes with you.

todo.task: Book Hakuba, 11-14 Oct
todo.remarks: Three nights on one base, arriving as the long weekend empties out — all three are ordinary weekday nights, which is the point of travelling on the holiday rather than before it. Ask about laundry.

todo.task: Book Matsumoto, 14-16 Oct
todo.remarks: Near the castle or the station both work; Nakamachi is the nicer evening walk.

todo.task: Book Nagano, 9-11 Oct
todo.remarks: Two nights, near Nagano Station — the Togakushi bus and the car both leave from there and Zenkoji is 15 minutes up the road. Both nights are inside the Sports Day weekend, so book early; Zenkoji will be busier than a normal afternoon and the dawn service is the quiet alternative.

todo.task: Book Tokyo, 21-23 Oct — and check they hold luggage
todo.remarks: Two nights now, not one — this is where the freed Okuhida night went. Shinagawa or Hamamatsucho, on the Haneda side. The whole last day depends on leaving the cases at the desk after checkout, so confirm it when booking rather than on the morning.

todo.task: Book Haneda airport hotel, 8 Oct
todo.remarks: Landing at 22:15 — pick something inside or shuttle-linked to the terminal.

todo.task: Book ANA NH886 / NH885
todo.remarks: Waiting on an ANA promotion. Times in the file are the current timetable as at Aug 2026; the Oct 2027 schedule should load around Nov 2026, so confirm them before committing the rest.

todo.task: Reserve Hokuriku Shinkansen seats, Tokyo to Nagano, 9 Oct
Reserve the Togakushi bus, 10 Oct
todo.remarks: Every seat on the Nagano-Togakushi bus is reserved and online booking opens a month ahead, so around 10 Sep 2027. Eleven departures a day in green season, JPY 1,550 pp each way. IC cards like Suica are not accepted — cash or a contactless Visa on board. The Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass was discontinued in 2025.

todo.task: Book the hire car, Nagano 11 Oct to Matsumoto 14 Oct
todo.remarks: The first of two hires. Four days, collected at Nagano Station and dropped at Matsumoto Station — same prefecture, so the one-way fee should be nil or near it; confirm that when booking rather than assuming. Azumino is visited on the drive down, so the car goes back at 16:00 on the 14th, before checking in at Matsumoto - no hotel parking needed there at all. Ask two more things at the desk: whether winter tyres are fitted by mid-October, since the Hakuba and Azumino roads run high, and whether an ETC card comes with it for the tolls.

todo.task: Book the second hire car, Matsumoto 16 Oct to Nakatsugawa 19 Oct
todo.remarks: Four days, and this one crosses prefectures — Nagano to Gifu — so a one-way fee applies where the first hire's did not: JPY 18,700 including tax for a passenger car from Matsumoto Ekimae to Nakatsugawa Ekimae, on Toyota's own simulator. Toyota's list rate for a compact is JPY 8,580 for the first 24 hours then JPY 7,260 a day. Collect at 09:30 on the 16th; return on the afternoon of the 19th at the Nakatsugawa Ekimae branch, two minutes from the station, which closes at 20:00 — the plan lands around 16:45 after Narai, so there are about three hours of slack. Ask about winter tyres by mid-October and an ETC card, and check the boot takes both cases with two people in the car, since not forwarding the luggage is half the reason for the hire.

todo.task: Check the Kiso valley train and bus times, 20 Oct
todo.remarks: The morning is the part to get right. Out: the 07:41 local from Nakatsugawa passes Nagiso at 08:11, for the 08:40 bus to Tsumago (JPY 330 train, JPY 300 bus). The next pairing is two hours later, 10:19 and 10:30; the 08:14 local, terminating at Nagiso, is a tight backup, and walking from Nagiso Station to Tsumago is about an hour. Confirm the 07:41 runs on a Wednesday — some trains on this line run on specific days only. Back: Magome to Nakatsugawa Station, JPY 800, 25 minutes, hourly from 12:50 to 16:50 plus 17:50 on weekdays and 18:15, so the return needs no planning. These are the current timetables — recheck against the 2027 ones.

todo.task: Reserve JR Shinano and Tokaido seats, Nakatsugawa to Tokyo, 21 Oct
todo.remarks: Two legs, changing at Nagoya. Book them together so the oversized-baggage slot lands on the Tokaido half.

todo.task: Check the green-season Nagano to Hakuba bus timetable
todo.remarks: This sets day 2, not the shinkansen. Alpico run it from Bus Stop No. 26 at Nagano Station East Exit, 75-80 minutes, JPY 2,200-2,400 pp paid to the driver. Green season is about seven departures a day against sixteen in winter, so pick the bus first and work the morning backwards from it.

todo.task: Measure the cases against the Tokaido 160 cm rule
todo.remarks: Only matters for the Nagoya to Tokyo leg on 21 Oct. Height + width + depth of 160-250 cm needs a free oversized-baggage slot reserved with the seat; without one it is a JPY 1,000 charge at the gate. The Hokuriku Shinkansen on day 2 has no such rule.

todo.task: Buy a return on the Hirayu–Kamikochi shuttle, 16 Oct
todo.remarks: Nothing to reserve, which is the point of going in and out through Hirayu: Nohi's shuttle cannot be booked in advance at all, so it is bought at the counter on the day. Take the return, JPY 2,800 per person against JPY 1,500 each way. The Matsumoto-bound bus is the opposite case — every seat reserved a month ahead since 2025 — and the plan no longer uses it.

todo.task: Confirm the Tsugaike gondola is running, 13 Oct
todo.remarks: It took a maintenance closure in late October in a recent year. Worth a look before fixing the Hakuba days.

todo.task: Buy Tsugaike tickets at a Seven-Eleven
todo.remarks: JPY 3,300 per person instead of JPY 3,700 at the gate, including park entry.

todo.task: Run tools/fetch_weather.py from late Sep 2027
todo.remarks: Open-Meteo forecasts about 16 days. Until then the figures are Oct 2025 stand-ins, tagged as such. Kamikochi has no verified coordinates and will stay blank regardless.

todo.task: Grant the second traveller access to this trip
todo.remarks: Landing page, Who can edit panel, owner only. Until their email is ticked against this slug the whole private side is invisible to them.

todo.task: Confirm who is travelling and fix the names
todo.remarks: Seeded as CMC and a placeholder. Edit people on the Overview page.

todo.task: Pack for a 1,700 m spread
todo.remarks: Tsumago is at about 400 m and the Shinhotaka ropeway tops out at 2,156 m, where there will likely be snow. Layers rather than a second coat.

todo.task: Check passport validity (6 months)
Arrange travel insurance covering hiking
todo.remarks: Happo Pond and the Nakasendo are walked rather than climbed, but check the policy does not exclude anything above 2,000 m.

todo.task: Plan the two Tokyo days, 22-23 Oct
todo.remarks: Both are deliberately open. Dropping the third Okuhida night put a whole free day at the Tokyo end, and the last day lost Shibuya and Asakusa because both have been seen on earlier trips — as have Shinjuku and Ueno. Ginza is spoken for on the 21st and Tokyo Station on the 23rd afternoon. The hotel is at the Shinagawa end, so the Yamanote's western half and the Yokosuka line out towards Kamakura are the cheap directions to think in.
